title: Sesame Chicken Noodles with Bok Choy & Greens
description: Salt held right back, since soy and oyster sauce carry it. Taste at the very end.

items.prep: slurried with a splash of water

items.item: sesame seeds, sliced spring onion, chilli flakes

steps.text: Cook the noodles ({{noodles}}) separately to packet, drain, and toss with a drop of oil so they do not clump.
Garlic ({{garlic}} cloves) and ginger (2–3cm) into the bowl. Chop 3 sec / Speed 7. Scrape down.
Add the neutral oil ({{oil}}) and mushrooms ({{mushrooms}}). Sauté 3 min / 120°C / Reverse / Soft stir, letting them brown so they do not water down the sauce.

Add the soy ({{soy}}), oyster sauce ({{oyster}}), honey ({{honey}}), vinegar ({{vinegar}}) and water ({{water}}). Add the chicken. Cook 8 min / 100°C / Reverse / Soft stir. Check a piece at 7 minutes, breast overcooks fast. Lift the chicken out and set aside.
Into the sauce: green beans ({{beans}}) and carrot, 4 min / 100°C / Reverse / Soft stir. Add the bok choy stems and capsicum, 2 min. Add the leaves, 1 min, just to wilt.
Stir the cornflour slurry ({{cornflour}}) through, 1 min / 90°C / Reverse / Soft stir, to thicken to a glaze.
Return the chicken, add the drained noodles and sesame oil ({{sesame-oil}}). Toss 1–2 min / Reverse / Soft stir, or tip into a big bowl and toss by hand to avoid breaking the noodles.
Finish with sesame seeds, spring onion and chilli. Adjust with a splash more soy or vinegar.

notes.title: Doneness
notes.text: Chicken breast wants 74°C in the thickest piece. Check it rather than relying on the 8-minute timing alone.

notes.title: Watch-point
notes.text: That is a lot of veg, so do not overfill the bowl. Pulling the chicken out buys room. The slurry is what gets you a glaze instead of a soup.

notes.title: Slurry
notes.text: Mix the cornflour with cold water first, then add it to the hot liquid. Straight in, it clumps.
